name: Aloo Gosht
description: Pakistani aloo gosht with beef or mutton and tender potato chunks simmered in a well-cooked onion-tomato masala and comforting gravy.
ingredients: 750 g beef or mutton, curry cut
4 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into large chunks
2 green chilies and fresh coriander, for garnish
method: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the sliced onions over medium heat until evenly golden rather than very dark.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and stir briefly, then add the meat and fry for several minutes until the pieces change colour and begin to brown at the edges.
Add the tomatoes, red chilli, turmeric, coriander, cumin and salt. Cook while stirring until the tomatoes break down and the masala loses its raw watery appearance.
Add about 2 cups hot water, cover and simmer gently until the meat is nearly tender. Check occasionally and add more hot water only if the pot becomes dry before the meat softens.
Add the potato chunks once the meat is close to tender, along with enough hot water for the desired gravy. Cover and continue cooking until both meat and potatoes are fully tender.
Uncover and simmer briefly if the gravy needs concentrating, stirring gently so the potatoes remain intact. Taste for salt and garnish with green chillies and coriander.
tips: Do not add potatoes too early or they may break down before the meat becomes tender.
Cook the onion-tomato masala until the raw tomato taste disappears before adding water.
storage: Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate covered. Reheat the portion being served until thoroughly hot.
